title: Operational envelope characterization of the T5 shock tunnel operating as a shock tube
author: Luigi Galvan Peceguini

advisors.name: André Fernando de Castro da Silva

abstract: Hypersonic flows present a series of complex phenomena, such as dissociation and ionization, which require very high enthalpies to appear. Besides, aspects which are already present in lower speed flows, for example viscous effects, occur more intensely. Therefore, the use of impulse ground test facilities, of which shock tubes and shock tunnels are the most noticeable, is called for. Such equipment may be upgraded with various methods to raise enthalpy, among which the combustion of a stoichiometric mixture of hydrogen and oxygen diluted in helium. This technique is employed on IEAv's T5 shock tunnel, which will be utilized on FAB's PROPHIPER project to test the 14-X prototype, which shall reach Mach 10 at 30 km altitude, in real scale. As a step towards making T5 operational, the combustion process in the tunnel's driver section, enclosed by a solid plate, was analyzed, using gaseous mixtures with 75% helium in volume and pressures from 11 to 61 bar, in order to verify the maximum pressure reached for each initial condition. It was con firmed that the combustion happened in the deflagration regime, as planned, despite the use of only eight spark plugs, as opposed to the 18 originally planned. Furthermore, some preliminary tests utilizing a diaphragm and with a vacuum present in the driven section were made, which indicated that, while the peak pressure reaches similar values to the ones seen on the closed section experiments, the combustion process is significantly more complex, and evolves differently depending on the diaphragm opening pressure. With that, it was concluded that T5 is ready for further characterization, which will enable the determination of which driver gas's initial pressure value must be used to reach the desired test section conditions.
